newsitem.title: UK: LME aluminium and lead weaken under pressure.
newsitem.headline: LME aluminium and lead weaken under pressure.

text.p: Base metal prices ended mostly weaker on Monday with speculative liquidation taking its toll on aluminium and lead, dealers said.
Aluminium tumbled below the $1,600 support level early in the day following Friday's weak close.
That move encouraged fund liquidation which pushed prices to a low of $1,583, dealers said.
Aluminium closed not far from there at $1,585, a decline of $18 against Friday's kerb close. First support was seen just around the corner at $1,580.
Despite aluminium's disappointing price performance, U.S. aluminium industry mill product orders were at their best since 1994, according to industry analyst Stewart Spector.
Three-months copper explored the bottom of its recent price range, although it bounced from its lows in the afternoon and finished just $8 easier at $2,231.
Dealers said volumes were light due to the Copper Club activities in New York this week, and the market exhibited no fresh features.
"Copper held at the $2,222/25 support level. It had a strong rally last week to $2,270 and now it has come back to the bottom of its range," a dealer noted.
The market was waiting for Tuesday's LME copper stocks data, which showed a sharp rise on Friday of 15,325 tonnes, he added.
Lead and zinc also bore the pain of fund liquidation although they also came off their lows, dealers said.
Lead tumbled more than $25 from Friday's kerb close to just under $650, hitting a fresh 15-1/2 month low.
It then bounced on light shortcovering and finished the day at $657, down $18.
Zinc, last at $1,175, rebounded from the day's lows of $1,166. But it was still $8 lower and vulnerable to the downside.
Nickel, showed greater resilience following early weakness and finished at $7,835, a gain of $35.
Early profit-taking and speculative liquidation had initially driven nickel to below $7,700 before it bounced higher, boosted by expectations of a inventory drawdown on Tuesday.
Tin was also firmer, ending the kerb at $5,920, up $45.
But alloy was last quoted at $1,495/50, versus $1,520/25.
